name: north-south barricade line of stacked sandbags seen from above: rows of bags each showing a bulging top and a short front, end face at the bottom
label: wasteland_ruins/barricade-v

surfaces.part: top bag/awning strip with vertical stripes
upper brown and grey sandbag course
green bag and mid brown bag courses

answer.evidence: The object is a tall vertical stack of lumpy sandbag courses seen face-on. Row 1 is a light line and row 2 a darker line, over a red-brown striped face in rows 3-6, so the top is only a 1-2 row rim with no real horizontal surface. Each bag course shows brown, grey or green fill with a few single-pixel highlights (rows 7, 17, 33, 42), which are details and not top planes. There are no front-edge lines with eave shadow, no ellipses and no visible contents. A dark gap in rows 22-29 reads as a vertical opening. The whole silhouette is a near-constant 16px-wide column, so it reads as a front elevation of stacked bags, not a 3/4 structure with a top surface. The structure kind also fits poorly, since this is a barricade line and not a gate, pavilion or building.

styleAnswer.evidence: The references are whole houses and the candidate is a narrow sandbag column, so the kind does not match and I judged craft only. Measured facts favour the candidate: 18 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10, and 0% near-flat coverage, the same as both references. Only 24% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so most outlines lean toward the neighbouring bag colour instead of being a uniform black line. That makes the outline mixed rather than near_black. By eye, each bag carries about 4 lightness steps (top highlight, body, shaded front, dark seam) with varied grey, green and brown bags and no large flat areas. This is slightly fewer steps than the 5-6 on the roof tiles, but the texture and density hold up next to the references without looking sticker-like.
